archetypes.name: line-number-drift
archetypes.rationale: Plan cites 15+ specific line numbers across launch-review.sh, launch-cursor-implement.sh, launch-cursor-ci.sh, and test files; recent commit #3270 modified ship-pr.sh and may have shifted neighboring lines in related scripts, causing edits at wrong locations.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each file in scope, verify that the plan's cited line numbers match the current file state: confirm the STDERR_SINK="" and RISK="" initializations are near the stated lines in launch-review.sh (near lines 111 and 652), the --risk) case appears at the cited locations (lines 131 and 672), and each *_launcher_append_outer_meta call site matches the plan's line references (lines 604 and 1028 in launch-review.sh, line 339 in launch-cursor-implement.sh, line 227 in launch-cursor-ci.sh). Also verify that the test file line ranges the plan targets for static-grep removal (test-collect-agent-retry.sh lines 815-821, test-launch-review.sh lines 1368-1390 and 2724-2742) still contain the patterns described. Report any discrepancy between the plan's line numbers and the actual current file as a plan defect requiring correction before implementation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: meta-write-sequence
archetypes.rationale: The plan's new test assertions require STDERR_SINK= to appear before OUTER_LAUNCHER= in .meta files; this ordering must be structurally guaranteed by run-external-agent.sh — if the write sequence is reversed or conditional, the assertions will be fragile or always-failing.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/run-external-agent.sh and trace the sequence of writes to the .meta output file, identifying where STDERR_SINK= is written relative to where the *_launcher_append_outer_meta call (which writes OUTER_LAUNCHER=) is issued. Determine whether STDERR_SINK= is always written first or only conditionally, and whether the ordering invariant the plan asserts is actually guaranteed by the code. If OUTER_LAUNCHER= is written before STDERR_SINK=, or if the ordering depends on runtime conditions not controlled by the tests, flag the plan's ordering-based assertions in test-launch-review.sh and test-collect-agent-retry.sh as structurally incorrect. Also verify that the referenced contract in scripts/test-run-external-agent.sh (case #19h) is consistent with what run-external-agent.sh actually does. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: codex-asymmetry-evidence
archetypes.rationale: Plan justifies skipping FINDING_6 edits in codex launchers by asserting they never call *_append_outer_meta; if either launch-codex-implement.sh or launch-codex-ci.sh does call the function, the plan is incomplete and those launchers also need the empty-arg fix.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/launch-codex-implement.sh and scripts/launch-codex-ci.sh in full and confirm they contain zero calls to any *_launcher_append_outer_meta or external_launcher_append_outer_meta variant; if either file does call the function, report the location as a plan gap requiring a symmetric FINDING_6 edit. Additionally verify that .claude/rules/external-tool-launcher-parity.md exists and that its content explicitly classifies the codex/cursor append-outer-meta asymmetry as intentional — not merely that the rule file exists but addresses a different asymmetry. If the rule is absent or does not cover this specific difference, flag the plan's justification for skipping codex edits as unsubstantiated. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
